examples.ko: 휴가 때 햇볕에 타서 피부가 구릿빛이 됐어요.
examples.en: I got tanned in the sun on vacation and my skin turned bronze.
Bronzed skin looks healthy.
That athlete's bronzed forearms look great.
I walked through the autumn fields tinted copper.
The old statue has a copper hue.
I saw a bronze-skinned surfer on the beach.

explain: 구리처럼 붉은 갈색을 띠는 색이에요. 햇볕에 보기 좋게 탄 피부를 말할 때 가장 자주 나오고, 보통 건강하고 멋진 느낌이에요. 사이시옷 때문에 '구리삗'으로 소리 나요.

phrases.en: A man with a sun-tanned face is smiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구릿빛 피부'보다 얼굴만 콕 집어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you mean just the face, rather than skin in general.

phrases.example: 여름 내내 바닷가에서 놀아서 구릿빛으로 탔어요.
phrases.en: I played at the beach all summer and got a bronze tan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구릿빛이 되다'보다 햇볕에 타는 과정을 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This focuses on the process of getting tanned in the sun.

phrases.en: The athlete's bronzed arms look strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔, 다리처럼 몸의 한 부분에도 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can attach it to body parts like arms and legs.

explain_en: It is the reddish brown of copper. It most often describes skin nicely tanned by the sun, usually with a healthy, attractive feel. Because of the 사이시옷, it is pronounced '구리삗'.

examples.en: I divided the dough into lumps and baked them.
I packed the snow into one lump.
I put a chunk of meat in the fridge.
I made a doll out of a lump of clay.
I broke the lump of soil with my hands.
The rice clumped together and tastes bad.

explain: '덩이'는 혼자 쓰기보다 '고깃덩이', '눈덩이', '흙덩이'처럼 다른 말 뒤에 붙는 경우가 많아요. 또 '한 덩이, 두 덩이'처럼 덩어리를 세는 단위로 써요. 비슷한 '덩어리'가 일상에서 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: I put the lump of meat into the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '덩이'를 다른 말 뒤에 붙인 합친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compound word with 덩이 attached to another word.

phrases.en: I broke the clod of soil with my hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흙이 뭉친 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for soil stuck together in a lump.
In daily life, 덩어리 is more common than 덩이.

explain_en: '덩이' is more often attached to another word, as in '고깃덩이', '눈덩이' and '흙덩이', than used alone. It is also a counter for lumps, as in '한 덩이, 두 덩이'. The similar '덩어리' is more common in daily speech.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 뺨이 불그스레해요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day, so my cheeks are slightly red.
The sky was tinged red by the sunset.
The thin, reddish lips were striking.
Maybe from embarrassment, that kid's face turned slightly red.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려 코끝이 불그스레하고 열이 나요.
examples.en: I caught a cold, so the tip of my nose is reddish and I have a fever.

examples.ko: 색은 불그스레하지만 맛은 별로 달지 않은 사과예요.
examples.en: It's an apple that looks reddish but is not very sweet.

explain: '빨갛다'보다 연하고 은은하게 붉은 느낌이라 얼굴, 뺨, 노을처럼 살짝 붉을 때 어울려요. 같은 뜻으로 '불그스름하다'도 쓰지만, 활용할 때는 '불그스레해요'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The apple skin is slightly red.

phrases.example: 술을 마셔서 얼굴이 불그스레한 사람이 많았어요.
phrases.en: Many people had flushed faces from drinking.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it becomes 불그스레한.

phrases.example: 저녁 햇빛 때문에 벽이 불그스레해 보여요.
phrases.en: The wall looks reddish because of the evening sunlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something looks that way.

explain_en: It is softer than '빨갛다' and suggests a faint redness, suitable for faces, cheeks, and sunsets. '불그스름하다' means about the same. The conjugation is '불그스레해요'.

examples.en: The apples ripened bright red in the autumn sun.
I was so embarrassed that my face turned bright red.

examples.ko: 새빨간 장미 한 송이를 선물로 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a single deep red rose as a gift.
My nose is bright red from the cold weather.
The sunset dyed the sky bright red.
I cried all night, so my eyes are swollen and bright red.

explain: '빨갛다' 앞에 '새-'가 붙어서 아주 짙고 선명한 빨강을 말해요. ㅎ불규칙이라서 '새빨개요', '새빨간', '새빨갛게'로 바뀌어요. 같은 계열의 '시뻘겋다'는 더 크고 거센 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 그 사람 말은 모두 새빨간 거짓말이었어요.
phrases.en: Everything that person said was a total lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금도 사실이 아닌 뻔한 거짓말을 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress a lie that has no truth in it at all.

explain_en: Adding '새-' to '빨갛다' gives a very deep, vivid red. It is a ㅎ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '새빨개요', '새빨간' and '새빨갛게'. The related '시뻘겋다' feels bigger and heavier.

en: to be widely known; to be widely spread

examples.en: That restaurant is the talk of the town for its taste.

examples.ko: 그 선생님에 대한 칭찬이 학교에 자자했어요.
examples.en: Praise for that teacher was all over the school.

examples.ko: 소문이 자자하던 가게에 드디어 가 봤어요.
examples.en: I finally visited the shop everyone had been talking about.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 헤어졌다는 소문이 자자한데 사실일까요?
examples.en: There's talk everywhere that the two broke up, but is it true?
They say that actor's popularity is huge overseas too.

examples.ko: 칭찬이 자자하면 누구나 한 번 가 보고 싶어져요.
examples.en: When the praise is everywhere, anyone wants to go once.

explain: '자자하다'는 '소문이 자자하다', '칭찬이 자자하다', '명성이 자자하다'처럼 소문, 평판과 관련된 말과만 붙어요. 좋은 소문에도 나쁜 소문에도 쓰지만 실제로는 칭찬이나 인기에 가장 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I went to a bakery with a great reputation.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form that describes a noun after it.

phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 입을 모아 칭찬한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many people are praising someone.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 노래 실력으로 명성이 자자했어요.
phrases.en: That singer was widely famous for his singing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름이나 평판이 널리 알려졌다는 뜻으로, 과거의 일은 '자자했어요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a name or reputation is widely known; use 자자했어요 for the past.

explain_en: '자자하다' only pairs with words about rumor or reputation, such as '소문이 자자하다', '칭찬이 자자하다' and '명성이 자자하다'. It works for both good and bad talk, but in practice it is used most for praise and popularity.
